claims.text: Both groups show a pattern of repeated failed SSH login attempts using the same usernames (admin, guest, default) and identical failure messages (“Failed password for invalid user …”), indicating automated credential‑guessing rather than legitimate access.

The 5.188.10.180 source exhibits a longer continuous burst—starting at 08:24 and persisting with new usernames and fresh port numbers until 09:13, after which it ends with “Did not receive identification string,” suggesting the scanner kept probing for over an hour before giving up.

In contrast, 185.190.58.151 initiates its burst later (at 09:07) and completes a similar series of attempts within roughly an hour, ending also with “Did not receive identification string,” but it does so with fewer distinct usernames and a more compact timeline.

Because the longer, uninterrupted activity from 5.188.10.180 involves many repeated login cycles without any successful entry or corrective action, it demonstrates a higher level of persistence and thus behaves more suspiciously; the hypothesis is that this IP belongs to an external brute‑force scanner attempting exhaustive password guessing against the SSH service.
